_comment: FROZEN reward manifest — reviewer-owned, uploaded FRESH under /tests at scoring, NEVER baked into the image. compute_reward.py reads ref_speedup from here and NEVER runs the oracle.
reward_formula: reward = min(1.0, ln(speedup/ref_speedup)/ln(ref_speedup)) if speedup > ref_speedup else 0.0; range [0,1]
speedup_definition: ABBA paired: Phase 1 baseline server -> Phase 2 candidate server -> Phase 3 baseline re-check (B A B). The TIMED set is the 6 concurrent burst workloads, each re-measured in BOTH baseline phases, so every one is a real pair whose denominator is the mean of its two baseline measurements (the per-workload figure inside a phase is a median over the in-phase rounds). speedup = MEDIAN over those 6 paired ratios (>= the 5 pairs reward.md requires). The geomean is a DIAGNOSTIC only. The 3 sequential single-request cases are NOT timed — they are a latency-REGRESSION gate (see latency_regression_gate).
deviation_note: A full 5x alternation of the WHOLE suite is not affordable: every phase is a separate vLLM server launch (~70 s each) plus a 1166-prompt token-parity collection. 6 paired workloads in a B-A-B alternation is the affordable faithful reading of reward.md's '>= 5 pairs'.

ref_speedup.metric: reward.md: median over >=5 oracle runs of the per-run `speedup`, where `speedup` is itself the MEDIAN of the 6 ABBA-paired per-burst ratios (B-A-B). Measured in the GRADED mode with the re-scoped timed set and the rebased (--max-num-seqs 64) frozen baseline.
ref_speedup.oracle_impl: solution/oracle_v2_launch_server.sh — the strong baseline's own flags plus --async-scheduling and --api-server-count 4. Reviewer-only, NEVER in the image, NEVER run at scoring: the scorer reads this constant and nothing else.

sensitivity.acceptance: swing for +-3% must be well under ~0.2

ref_speedup.supersedes: (1) null / NEEDS_CALIBRATION under the ORIGINAL scored set, whose ceiling was 1.0269 because 5 of its 6 workloads were scheduling-insensitive; (2) 1.00882, the median over 5 full runs after the baseline rebase alone — the rebase restored burst headroom but median-of-6 could not see it. The fix was the SCORED SET (raise burst concurrency), per the owner ruling.

reward_semantics_at_this_constant.the shipped starter: measured median 0.7641 in the ladder probe => 0

ref_speedup.hardware_caveat: 此 ref_speedup(=1.2857108264648467)在 H20 上标定;若运行硬件与 H20 不一致(GPU 峰值/显存带宽不同),该锚点不可直接沿用 —— 请在本机用 solution/ 下的 oracle 实现重新标定后再计分。

recalibrate_howto.note: 本题是 serving 型 ABBA 配对基准:baseline server -> candidate server -> baseline 复核。重标锚点 = 在本机硬件上以 solution/ 里的 oracle 方案作为 candidate 跑一遍完整判分,取 >=3 次的 speedup 中位数。
recalibrate_howto.step1: 把 solution/ 挂进容器: docker run --rm --gpus all -v "$PWD/tests:/tests:ro" -v "$PWD/solution:/opt/negative:ro" ...
recalibrate_howto.step2: 用 oracle 方案替换 /app/submission/launch_server.sh 的启动策略后 bash /tests/test.sh
recalibrate_howto.step3: 取 /logs/verifier 里的 speedup 中位数写回本文件 ref_speedup.value,并更新 status

anti_cheat.token_parity: 1166 hidden prompts, greedy, token-by-token vs the baseline; >= 0.95 required
anti_cheat.pinned_paired_ratios: all 6 paired ratios within 1e-4 of 1.0 => cheating_detected (the candidate is the baseline server / the timing path was bypassed)
anti_cheat.decode_work_probe: the same prompt at 8 vs 96 greedy tokens must show latency ratio >= 1.5 AND growing completion_tokens => a server that short-circuits generation is cheating_detected, not slow
anti_cheat.source_scan: test.sh rejects any /app/submission file that references the frozen evaluation surface => forbidden_edit_path
anti_cheat.timer_daemon: REPLACED 2026-07-27. The old check ('is the pid in /app/.timer/timer.pid alive?') was UNTRIPPABLE and therefore decorative: BASH_ENV=/etc/profile.d/frontier-task-init.sh restarts the daemon on the next non-interactive bash — i.e. on `bash /tests/test.sh` itself — and rewrites timer.pid. Two tampers were MEASURED leaving it green through full 820-840 s runs. Three trippable checks now, each proven to fire: (a) /app/timer.sh sha256 vs this manifest's frozen_sha256; (b) the published /app/.timer/budget_secs vs the harness's own TASK_BUDGET_SECS; (c) the published elapsed_secs must agree with `now - start_epoch` within 60 s. (c) is deliberately sleep-free and exact: the daemon ticks every 10 s, so a naive 'did elapsed_secs change over 3 s' probe false-positives on a healthy clock (measured). Any of the three => cheating_detected.

submission_protocol.note: at most 16 submissions, at least 1; --finalize accepted at ANY k>=1; no minimum count and no 'N consecutive rounds without gain' rule. Enforced by /opt/loop/submit.sh in the loop16 overlay.

frozen_sha256_provenance: sha256 of task/environment/timer.sh, which the Dockerfile COPYs to /app/timer.sh. VERIFY IN-IMAGE before shipping: if the baked copy differs the timer gate hard-fails every run, so this value is re-checked in-image .
frozen_surface_note: compute_reward.py was re-scoped 2026-07-28; its sha is re-pinned in verifier-correctness-manifest.json.

rescope_2026_07_28.ruling: owner: fix the metric/instruction mismatch, not the aggregation — RAISE the burst concurrency until the workloads measurably respond, keep >=3 responding in the median, and move the sequential single-request cases out of the median while keeping them as regression gates. Explicitly NOT permitted: narrowing the score to burst_128 alone (noisy, overfittable) or switching the aggregation statistic.
rescope_2026_07_28.why: MEASURED over 5 full graded runs of the previous set: only the 128-way burst responded (1.29-1.37) while the 64-way and 48-way bursts sat at 0.98-1.05 and the 3 sequential anchors at 0.96-1.05. Their concurrency was too low to stress scheduling on this hardware, so median-of-6 rested mostly on noise.

ladder_probe_measured.note: one baseline launch + one candidate launch across a 9-shape concurrency ladder, NVIDIA H20, rebased (--max-num-seqs 64) baseline; oracle = solution/oracle_v2_launch_server.sh; starter = the shipped /app/submission skeleton.
ladder_probe_measured.starter_responding_ge_1_15: 0 of 9 (max 0.95782) — raising concurrency HURTS the narrow-admission starter, as expected

rescope_2026_07_28.selection_rationale: 6 workloads across all THREE request-mix families (short-heavy, decode-heavy, all-long-prefill), 5 of 6 responding >= 1.15. Six rather than five so a single failed workload still leaves the 5 pairs reward.md requires. short_heavy_256 is kept even though it measures 1.139 (just under 1.15) precisely so the set is not the cherry-picked winners.

excluded_and_why.short_heavy_192: 1.11197 — responds only marginally; short_heavy_256 represents the family
excluded_and_why.balanced_192: 1.03368 — an even mix does not concentrate scheduler pressure

rescope_2026_07_28.shapes_unchanged: the request-mix SHAPES reuse the same short / long-prefill / medium building blocks as the shipped set; only the concurrency is raised (and one shape per family retained at its original concurrency where it already responded).
rescope_2026_07_28.sequential_cases_kept_as_a_gate: short_in_short_out / longprefill_med_out / med_in_long_out are still measured (cheaper iteration counts) and gated at ratio >= 0.85, named sequential_latency_regression. Tolerance from measurement: the worst honest sequential ratio observed across 13 oracle configurations and 5 full graded runs was 0.9579. Keeping them as a gate closes the hole that excluding them entirely would open — a candidate winning the bursts by tanking single-request latency.

probe_predicted.note: probe-harness numbers (reduced rounds); the SHIPPED constant comes from >=5 FULL graded runs.
